newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins consolidate after rise on US rates.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins consolidate after rise on US rates.

text.p: Prices of Russian MinFin bonds consolidated at new levels after profit-taking on Wednesday, having firmed in early trading on relief that U.S. interest
The U.S. Federal Reserve announced on Tuesday that it would not change interest rates. But analysts said the possibility of a rise in July could still hang over the market.
MinFins, along with other emerging debt, are sensitive to any news which would suggest a change in U.S. interest rates and consequently affect U.S. Treasury bond prices.
"We have seen an upward trend as the market felt relief," Eurobank dealer Olivier Coursault said. "But it was not really bullish as there may be a rate hike next time."
Dealers said the third and fourth tranches were the most actively traded.
"Prices started to rise in the morning on the (U.S. interest) rate news," a Russian bank dealer said. "But London was later seen trying to gain buying the fourth tranche and selling the third one."
The 1999 and 2003 maturities met support at 87.70 and 63.00 respectively.
"Everything is firm but there is no real bullish trend as we have seen a little bit of profit-taking," Coursault said.
